Concrete Pool Decks · Siesta Key, FL

Concrete Pool Deck Installation on Siesta Key

A concrete pool deck on Siesta Key runs $5–$15 per sq ft installed as of October 2026. A deck close to the Gulf has to clear two separate lines: the county's own Gulf Beach Setback Line and Florida's statewide Coastal Construction Control Line.

By the Opera Concrete & Pavers estimating team · Updated October 1, 2026

Picture a 24 × 28 ft pool deck, 672 sq ft, on a Gulf-front lot close enough to the dune to raise the setback question

Picture a 24 × 28 ft pool deck, 672 sq ft, on a Gulf-front lot close enough to the dune to raise the setback question. Pricing it at $5–$15 per sq ft lands between $3,360 and $10,080, settling near $4,704 to $8,064 inside the typical $7–$12 band for a textured, slip-resistant surface pitched to a drain. Before that figure firms up, a current survey confirms where the Gulf Beach Setback Line and the state's control line actually fall on this particular parcel, since storm-driven sand movement since 2024 means an older survey may no longer match the ground as it sits today.

Two lines, not one, near the dune

Sarasota County's own Gulf Beach Setback Line bars "Construction or Excavation" seaward of it or waterward of the Barrier Island Pass Hazard Line specifically on Siesta, Casey and Manasota Keys, and a project inside that zone needs its own coastal setback variance from the county Sarasota County Code §54-723. That county line sits in addition to, not instead of, the state's Coastal Construction Control Line permit, which DEP requires for "construction and excavation activities seaward of the CCCL" FDEP's CCCL program. A deck that clears one line but not the other still can't be built, so both get checked before a design is drawn.

What a Kool Deck-Style Coating Actually Is

A spray texture or Kool Deck-style coating is not a structural pour, it's a thin acrylic cement topping troweled or sprayed over a cured concrete base slab to add texture, color and some heat reflectance. Market ranges put that coating at roughly $3 to $6 per square foot in Central Florida, well under the $5 to $15 per square foot a full new concrete pour runs. A Siesta Key homeowner resurfacing instead of replacing is paying for surface texture and color, not a new slab underneath, so a coating only makes sense when the base concrete is still structurally sound, without the cracking or settling that signals a deeper problem.

What storm-shifted sand changed about where that line sits

Hurricane Milton's October 2024 landfall near the island, and the surge from Hurricane Helene 13 days before it, pushed enough sand around on some stretches of beach that the practical edge of the setback line has moved on certain lots since the last survey most homeowners have on file Mysuncoast.com, Hurricane Milton landfall near Siesta Key. We pull a current survey rather than rely on an older plat before pricing a deck addition anywhere near the dune, since the setback line itself, not just the sand on top of it, can have shifted.

Why the Pool Excavation Itself Is the Best Soil Test You'll Get

A pool excavation digs deeper into the ground than almost any other part of a Siesta Key project, which makes it the clearest look at actual soil conditions anyone on the job gets before the deck base goes in. If the hole hits standing water or visibly wet soil shallower than the published range for the area's dominant soil series suggests, we treat the deck base around that side of the pool as wet-soil work and add the extra 2 to 4 inches ICPI calls for, rather than assuming one soil reading applies evenly on every side of the same excavation.

Settling Near the Coping Isn't the Same as Pool Structure Movement

A dish-shaped low spot in the deck, away from the coping itself, is almost always ordinary settling from a base that lost compaction, the same failure mode any slab can show, not a sign of movement in the pool shell underneath it. True structural movement in the pool itself is rare and shows up differently, usually as cracking inside the pool's interior finish rather than in the surrounding deck. That same high-claim list state regulators publish for sinkholes names Orange County but leaves out Sarasota and Manatee. A Siesta Key homeowner seeing a soft spot away from the pool edge should expect a base and drainage fix, not a structural pool inspection.

The Last Step: Checking Every Drain and Joint Before Cleanup

Once the deck is finished and cured, we walk every deck drain and the full length of the isolation joint before calling the job done, checking that water actually moves toward the drains rather than pooling against the coping anywhere around the pool. On a Siesta Key job, this walk-through happens with a hose running water across sections that don't get an obvious test from rain alone, since a dry-season completion can hide a slope problem the first wet season would otherwise reveal. Catching a low spot at this stage means a quick patch, not a callback after the homeowner has already furnished the deck.

Watching the Isolation Joint's Sealant Over Time

The flexible sealant in a pool deck's isolation joint takes the brunt of the deck and the pool shell moving independently, year after year, and it wears out well before the concrete on either side of it does. A Siesta Key homeowner who checks that joint once or twice a year for cracking, gaps or sections where the sealant has pulled away from either surface catches a failing joint while a simple recaulk still fixes it. Letting a failed isolation joint go unaddressed defeats the whole purpose of having built it in the first place, since water and debris start working into exactly the gap the deck needed protected.

Frequently asked questions

Does my Siesta Key pool deck need a county permit, a state permit, or both?

Possibly both. The county's Gulf Beach Setback Line requires its own variance for work seaward of it, and Florida's separate Coastal Construction Control Line adds a DEP permit requirement on top, independent of each other.

Did Hurricane Milton move the beach setback line on Siesta Key?

On some lots, the storm surge and sand movement from the October 2024 landfall shifted where the practical edge of the setback sits, which is why we check a current survey rather than an older one before designing a deck near the dune.

What's the Barrier Island Pass Hazard Line?

A second boundary the county names alongside the Gulf Beach Setback Line, specific to Siesta, Casey and Manasota Keys, and construction or excavation waterward of either one needs a coastal setback variance.
